memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: 'Then at the entrance to the tent of meeting, the Nazirite must shave off the hair that symbolizes their dedication. They are to take the hair and put it in the fire that is under the sacrifice of the fellowship offering. After the Nazirite has shaved off the hair of their dedication, the priest is to place in their hands a boiled shoulder of the ram, and one thick loaf and one thin loaf from the basket, both made without yeast.' - Num 6:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At the close of the vow, the Nazirite shaved off the hair that had marked their dedication and placed it in the fire of the fellowship offering. The very sign of their commitment was given up to God in the flames. Their whole devotion, from beginning to end, was offered to the Lord.

There is something tender in this picture. The long hair had been the visible symbol of a season of special nearness to God. Now, at the end, even that symbol was surrendered to Him. Nothing was held back for the person to keep as a trophy. It all went to God.

This teaches us that our devotion, from start to finish, belongs to the Lord. We do not serve God to gain something to boast about later. Even our seasons of deep dedication are gifts we give back to Him, not achievements we cling to.

And notice the gentleness of the ending: the priest placed food into the Nazirite's hands — the shoulder of the ram, the loaves of bread. After a season of giving up, there was now a receiving, a shared meal, a moment of fellowship and provision. God does not leave His devoted ones empty; He fills their hands.

However your seasons of devotion unfold, offer them fully to God. And trust that the God who receives your surrender also fills your hands with His good gifts and His fellowship.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you offer your devotion fully to God, holding nothing back?
- Do you cling to spiritual "trophies," or surrender all to Him?
- How has God filled your hands after seasons of giving up?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I offer my whole devotion to You, holding nothing back as my own. Thank You that You fill the hands of those who surrender to You. Amen.
